chapters.title: Why it really ended (your side of it)
chapters.teaser: Not who was right. What your soul was doing while it fell apart.

chapters.title: Your breakup pattern
chapters.teaser: How you end things, how you grieve, and the habit that slows you down.

chapters.title: Why you keep checking
chapters.teaser: What the pull back toward them is really asking for.

chapters.title: So, will they come back? The honest answer
chapters.teaser: What a chart can and can't tell you, and the question that matters more.

chapters.title: If they ever reach out
chapters.teaser: Three questions to ask before you reply, built for your soul.

chapters.title: What you do now
chapters.teaser: The next small steps that help, whatever they decide.

text.why-it-ended: Eul Wood is the vine, the flower, the plant that finds light through a crack in the pavement. You adapt beautifully. In your last relationship you probably adapted a little too well. You bent around their schedule, their moods, their friends, until the shape of you got hard to find. Maybe they lost interest in someone who always agreed. Maybe you got tired of being flexible and never chosen. Either way, the ending likely came after a long quiet stretch of you saying it's fine when it wasn't. That's the part worth looking at. Not to blame yourself, but to remember that your needs were in the room too.
text.your-breakup-pattern: Your breakups are rarely clean. Eul Wood doesn't cut, it untangles, one tendril at a time. You stay friends, or try to. You keep the shared playlist. You still ask after their mum. Part of this is genuine kindness, and it's lovely. Part of it is that you hate leaving anything with nowhere to grow. The risk is keeping a doorway open so long that you never fully step into your own life. Some vines need to let go of the old fence to find a better wall. And you are far tougher than you look. You've survived things that would flatten a tree.
text.the-pull: For you, the pull is connection itself. You're wired to wind around someone, and when that someone is gone, the empty space feels almost physical. You might catch yourself watching their stories, rereading old chats, asking mutual friends casual questions that are not casual at all. It isn't weakness. It's a plant reaching for the last light it knew. Try reaching somewhere new on purpose. Text a friend before you open their profile. Make a plan that has nothing to do with romance. Your heart doesn't need them specifically. It needs warmth, and warmth lives in more than one place.
text.the-honest-answer: Here's the truth Bom and Yeon agree on: nobody can tell you what another person will decide. Their heart isn't in your chart. What is in your chart is your habit of making yourself smaller to keep the peace. If you went back, would you go back as yourself, or as the version that bends? That's the real question. Eul Wood thrives where flexibility goes both ways. If you were always the one bending, wanting them back may really mean wanting all that effort to finally pay off. You can let the effort go and keep the lesson. The lesson is the part that travels with you.
text.if-they-reach-out: If they ever reach out, your first impulse will be warmth. You'll want to make it easy for them. Pause on that. Before you reply, write down one thing you needed and didn't get last time. Just one. Then notice whether their message leaves room for it. Are they asking how you are, or asking to be comforted? Reconnecting is allowed. So is a friendly I'm glad you're doing well, and nothing more. The key for Eul Wood is choosing instead of drifting. If you move toward them, move on purpose, with your needs said out loud from the very first conversation.
text.what-you-do-now: Repot yourself. New routine, a new corner of the city, new people around you. Eul Wood flourishes quickly in good conditions, so build some on purpose. Spend time with friends who let you talk without fixing you. Try something social and low stakes: a class, a club, a group run. Notice your own preferences, even tiny ones, like what you order when nobody else decides first. Then say them. That practice, boring as it sounds, is what changes your next relationship most. You are not hard to love. You've just been easy to overlook, sometimes even by you.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You gave so much, Eul. Being soft isn't why it ended.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: No, but saying it's fine forty times probably didn't help.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Missing them is just your heart looking for warmth.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then text a friend. Their stories are not a heater.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Next time, bring your needs to the table first.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You bend beautifully. Now practise not bending. Just once. For fun.

spring.intro: Spring-born Eul Wood came up in the greenest month of the year, surrounded by other growing things. Wood was in charge, which gave your vine plenty of support and plenty of competition. In love that shows up as attachment that wraps fast and wraps well. You knew their friends, their coffee order, their mum's birthday. When it ended, you didn't lose one person, you lost a whole trellis. That's why it feels so structural. Spring vines also re-root easily, which can be a blessing or a trap: the easiest wall to climb is the one you already know. Before you reach back toward the old trellis, ask whether you miss them or miss being held up.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You don't miss them. You miss the wall you were climbing. Different problem.

summer.intro: Summer Eul Wood is a flower in full bloom, which looks gorgeous and costs a lot. Fire commanded your birth season and Wood feeds Fire, so your energy naturally flows out as charm, warmth and visible effort. In the relationship you likely made everything look effortless while working hard behind the scenes. Then the breakup, and suddenly nobody's watching the bloom. Summer flowers wilt when they're over-exposed: too many updates, too many friends asking, too much replaying out loud. You might be performing okay-ness on your stories while privately checking theirs. Shade is not hiding. Give yourself a few quiet weeks where you're not blooming for anyone, especially an audience of one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Posting a glowing selfie for one specific viewer is not healing, Eul.

autumn.intro: Autumn hits a flower harder than a tree. Metal ruled when you were born, Eul Wood, and Metal is the element that controls and cuts Wood. You grew up under a season of pressure, which made you adaptable and very good at reading what others expect. In love you likely bent around them: their schedule, their moods, their version of events. The breakup might have felt like the shears finally closing. Here's the autumn secret: vines survive cutting better than almost anything. You will grow back. What matters is where. Not toward someone who made you smaller to fit. Toward a support that holds you without pruning you every week.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Vines grow back stronger after cutting. You're already sending out new shoots.

winter.intro: Winter Eul Wood is the bulb under frozen ground: quiet, patient, holding the whole flower inside. Water rules winter and nourishes Wood, so you have deep emotional reserves, but cold water also keeps you still. After the breakup you probably retreated inward, replaying conversations with the attention of a novelist. You feel everything and show almost nothing. That can make an ex think you didn't care, when really you cared in a season where nothing shows above ground. The pull for you is memory. You revisit it because it's warm in there. Bring a little Fire into your days: sunlight, a loud friend, a plan with a date on it. Bulbs need warmth to remember they're flowers.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You cared more than you showed. That's winter, not coldness.

strength.strong: Eul, your chart surrounds your vine with support, which makes you resilient and quietly determined. You don't let go easily. In a breakup that can turn into persistence that looks like hope: one more message, one more chance, one more look at their page. You can wind around a closed door for a long time. The blind spot is mistaking grip for love. Strong vines can choke what they cling to. Notice if you're holding on because they were right for you or because letting go feels like losing. Loosening your grip is still strength.
strength.weak: With little support in your chart, Eul, you grew by leaning on whatever was nearby, and in love you probably leaned hard. You adapted to their tastes, their friends, their timetable, until your own shape got blurry. After the breakup you might feel you don't know who you are without them. That feeling is real, and it passes. You weren't empty. You were wrapped around someone else's frame. Spend the next weeks finding supports that are yours: a class, a friend group, a habit. Grow back toward yourself before toward anyone.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and answers, even in heartbreak. You want a plan for getting over it, maybe even a plan for getting them back. Slow down. Not everything grows on schedule, and some things need to just sit for a while. Ask for help instead of turning healing into a project. For balance, let a little Metal in: declutter, finish old things, clear out the drafts folder. A clean edge helps Wood stop reaching for what's already gone.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means fresh starts feel heavy. After a breakup you might stay in the same place, emotionally and literally, for longer than you'd like. That isn't weakness. It just means new growth needs a nudge. Small steps work best: a new route to work, one new class, one new person a week. Get outside in the mornings and keep something green near you. You don't need a whole new life. You need one new branch, and then another.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes you feel everything at full volume. A breakup can feel like an emergency, with urges to text, post, or fix it all tonight. Your passion is real, but heat isn't a strategy. Before any big move, sleep on it. Cool down with water: swimming, long showers, quiet evenings at home. Talk to your calmest friend before your most exciting one. Let the fire warm you instead of burning through your peace.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means joy and visibility don't come easily, and after a breakup you might go dim for a while, hiding from people and from fun. Turn the lights back on gently. Sunshine, music, dancing in the kitchen, one social plan a week even when you'd rather stay in. Letting people see you is the medicine here. Warmth doesn't only live in romance. It's in friends, in laughter, in simply being out in the world.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you hold on: to routines, to memories, to the hope that things will settle back into their old place. Stability is your gift, but in heartbreak it can turn into staying stuck. Shake the ground a little. Move the furniture, take a short trip, try something unplanned. Let some Wood energy in, growth and new beginnings. You can keep what was good and still leave room for something new to grow.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means life can feel unsteady, and a breakup can knock away what little ground you had. You might feel scattered, unsure where to put your feet. Build structure gently: regular meals, a steady bedtime, one place at home that's only yours. Cook something. Walk somewhere. Lean on the people who are reliable. Stability first, big decisions later. You need solid ground under you before deciding anything about the past.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal makes you sharp and decisive, sometimes too quickly. You may have cut the relationship off cleanly and then refused to look at what you feel. Or you judge yourself harshly for every mistake you made in it. Soften the edges. Let Water in: rest, tears, music, journaling. Feeling the grief isn't the same as reopening the door. You can keep your boundaries firm and still let your heart thaw.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard, so after a breakup you might keep the door half open, answer every message, or stay friends when it hurts. Practise clean edges. Mute without guilt. Box up their things. Say no without explaining. White and silver, tidy spaces and finished tasks all help your chart. A boundary isn't cold. It's how you protect the part of you that's still healing.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means you think and feel deeply, maybe endlessly. After a breakup you might drift through memories, analyse every detail, and lose sleep to what-ifs. Your intuition is a gift, but it needs riverbanks. Add some Earth: routines, cooking, walks, people who ground you. Give overthinking a time limit. Feel it fully, then get up and do one ordinary thing.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means rest and reflection get skipped. You may rush past the breakup, staying busy so you never have to sit with it. That works until suddenly it doesn't. Build in quiet on purpose: slow mornings, water by your bed, a few lines in a journal at night, a bath instead of another plan. Let yourself feel without fixing. Intuition grows when you give it some silence.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: So much Wood. You've drafted three versions of 'hey, random but' already.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy wants a goal. Give it your own plans, not their inbox.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: every feeling is a five-alarm emergency. It's a breakup, not an inferno.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is beautiful. Let it cool before you hit send on anything.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth. You'd still be in that relationship purely out of habit.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Just make sure you're loyal to yourself too.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. You cut them off cleanly, then reread everything at midnight.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Being firm protected you. Being gentle with yourself will heal you.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've cried to three songs and written a novel in your notes app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Feeling deeply is a gift. Just come up for air sometimes.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make moving on feel stuck. Small new routines count as growth.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: You haven't changed anything since the breakup, including your lock screen. Start there.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make joy feel far away. Borrow some from a loud friend.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: You stopped having fun when they left. Fun was never theirs to take.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth can make everything feel unsteady. Simple routines will hold you.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no anchor. You re-decide whether to text them every hour.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal makes boundaries tricky. You're allowed to say no to your own phone.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means you'll answer at 2am. Put the phone in another room.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make grief hide. It's okay to let it surface slowly.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: You said you're fine twelve times today. Water would like a word.

gap-wood.title: The tree and the vine that let go
gap-wood.text: You loved a Gap Wood, which means you loved a person who answered ten messages with one decisive sentence. You sent the song, the meme, the long voice note about your weird day, and you got back 'haha nice' and a plan for Saturday. You told yourself the plan was the love. Sometimes it was. Here's the part that stings: you bent so smoothly around their certainty that they may never have known you disagreed. You said 'sure, sounds good' and then quietly did the opposite, and when they found out, they called it dishonest, and you felt caught for having a want at all. Vines learn to go around walls. You just never got to be the wall for once. The pull is the shade they gave. They were steady, and steady is hard to find when your own feelings move like weather. But steadiness you had to tiptoe around was never quite shelter. Try this: say one blunt, unpadded sentence to someone this week. 'I don't want to go.' 'I liked that.' Notice that you survive it. That's the muscle worth building, whoever ends up next to you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'Ok' was not a love letter, Gap. It wasn't a breakup text either.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, your voice notes were adorable. You were allowed to want more than one sentence back.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Next time, say the thing before the sticker.

eul-wood.title: Two vines, no gardener
eul-wood.text: Two Eul Woods in love make the sweetest group chat in the world. Voice notes at lunch, stickers at midnight, 'omg same' to everything. You understood each other's moods without explanation. And then came a decision. Where to live. Whether to move in. Even where to eat on a Friday, which could take forty minutes and end at the same noodle place anyway. Neither of you wanted to be the one who chose, because choosing means you might be blamed. Big topics got dodged inside cute messages. Small irritations leaked out sideways, as jokes to friends or quiet comparisons. You both wanted the other's approval so much that honesty felt risky. The ending, if you look closely, probably wasn't a decision either. It was a drift, two vines slowly growing toward different walls. That's why it's so hard to grieve: there's no moment to point at, no night you can circle on the calendar. The pull is how easy it felt. Nobody else got your humour that fast. What helps now is practising deciding. Small things, out loud, without asking anyone. 'We're getting dumplings.' A vine that can choose its own wall is the one that blooms.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You two were so kind to each other. Kind enough to never disagree, which is its own problem.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Forty minutes to pick dinner. Every week. I rest my case.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Choose one small thing today, out loud. Your future self will be grateful.

byeong-fire.title: The flower that faded in full sun
byeong-fire.text: You turned toward your Byeong Fire ex like a flower toward the sun, and for a season you bloomed. They were loud, generous, endlessly fun. Heart emojis by the dozen. Calls instead of texts. Parties where they knew everyone and pulled you into the light. But suns don't notice the edges of the room, and you started fading there. They forgot the plan you'd mentioned twice. They told your story better than you at dinner. You tried subtle ways to be seen, a slightly cooler reply, a post they might notice, and they read it as games and got frustrated. You weren't ignored, exactly. You were warmly overlooked, which is much harder to explain to your friends. The pull is the glow. Life with them felt like a permanent golden hour, and your own days look dimmer by comparison. What you can practise is being seen on purpose, without hints. Tell someone directly, 'I want to share something, can I have five minutes?' People who love you will give it gladly. And you'll learn you never needed to wilt to be noticed.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, a hundred heart emojis can't fix forgetting their plans twice.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, you were allowed to just say 'I need you to notice me.'

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Too much sun scorches. Hints in the shade get missed. Both fixable.

jeong-fire.title: Flowers by candlelight, never said aloud
jeong-fire.text: This one was soft and romantic, and almost nothing important got said out loud. You and your Jeong Fire ex wrote each other long, careful messages and read between every line. You went vague when something hurt. They went quiet. Resentment sat under the candlelight like a draught you could feel but never find. They wanted your attention focused, intensely, on them, and you love a wide circle of friends, so every brunch you went to alone felt to them like a small betrayal and to you like a small cage. You both worried, and together you made the worry bigger: two yin souls whispering the worst-case version to each other at 1am. The hurt here is gentle and long. Nothing exploded. It just got harder to breathe. The intimacy is what you miss. Nobody else listened to your feelings with that much care. Try saying one direct thing, in daylight, to someone you love. Not a hint. Not a meme. 'That upset me.' It feels clumsy. It's also how you stop needing a code to be understood.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, your love was real. It just needed more than one person to hold it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, 'it's nothing' was never nothing. You both knew.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Agree on a code word for 'I'm actually upset.' Then actually use it.

mu-earth.title: The vine that couldn't move the mountain
mu-earth.text: You tried everything a vine knows to move a mountain: charm, hints, a playful text, a clever workaround. Your Mu Earth ex didn't budge. Not out of meanness. Mountains just don't. You texted often, playfully; they replied late and short, with full sincerity, and you read 'ok' as boredom when it was, honestly, affection in its natural state. You found them emotionally slow. They found you socially busy, always another plan, another group, another idea. When you couldn't change something directly, you went around it, and they noticed, and noticing made them dig in harder. That's what made it so tiring: you spent the whole relationship climbing and never quite reaching the top. Their steadiness is the hook. In a life where everything shifts, they were the one fixed thing, and part of you misses having something to hold. Ask yourself honestly whether you miss them, or miss the climb. Then borrow the mountain's trick for a week: say no once, plainly, and don't apologise for it. Standing still is a skill too, and it suits you more than you think.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, a single heart emoji would have changed so many evenings.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, their 'ok' was warm. It just wasn't decorated.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Charm doesn't move mountains. Honest asks sometimes do.

gi-earth.title: The vine in the garden bed
gi-earth.text: Your Gi Earth ex was the garden bed, and you grew so well in it that you forgot to check how the soil was doing. They asked practical questions: did you pay the bill, did you eat, what time is the train. You sent feelings and fun and the occasional voice note about a dream you had. They wanted answers to the real stuff; you thought they were nagging. When they worried, you called it overthinking. Both of you dislike direct conflict, so nothing got said. They felt used, quietly. You felt managed, quietly. And two quiet people can let a garden go to weeds without either of them touching a single tool. You didn't realise how much they carried until they put it down, and that realisation arrived late and all at once. What pulls you back is the nurture. Nobody made you feel looked after like that. Notice who in your life does invisible work for you right now. A parent, a flatmate, a friend. Thank them specifically. And answer the boring practical question first next time. It's the most romantic thing a vine can learn.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, you're not 'too much' for worrying. You care in practical ways.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, someone kept you fed for months. Did you say thanks?

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Who gets the nutrients? Next time, both of you.

gyeong-metal.title: The vine wrapped around the blade
gyeong-metal.text: This was a Heavenly Combination, the vine wrapping the blade, and you probably felt the pull from the first night. Your Gyeong Metal ex was strong, protective, decisive in all the places you hesitate. You softened them; they made you feel safe. But Gyeong is a blade, and sometimes it cut. 'Where are you.' No question mark. Their bluntness landed deep, and you, being a vine, went around it: a sticker, a voice note about a cat, an answer that wasn't quite an answer. They wanted straight lines; you gave curves. When hurt, they got harsher and you got slipperier, and the closer you were, the worse it felt. That's why this ending is so loud in your head: it was a real fit, with a real flaw. You miss the protection most. You felt chosen by someone who doesn't choose easily. So practise straight answers. When someone asks where you are, say where you are, then send the cat. Directness isn't you turning into metal. It's you trusting that you're strong enough to be clear.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, 'Where are you.' with a full stop reads like a threat.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, a straight answer first, then the cat. They'd have loved both.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: A great match with a sharp edge. Sheath it, don't break it.

sin-metal.title: Pruned by the scissors
sin-metal.text: You were with someone who thought they were helping you grow in the right direction. Your Sin Metal ex had taste, precision, an eye for detail you admired, and they aimed it at you. A comment about your outfit. A suggestion about your friend. A small edit to how you told a story. Each one was minor and beautifully phrased, and each one felt like a snip. You adapted, because adapting is what vines do, and they saw your flexibility as a lack of backbone, which only invited more pruning. Both of you held grudges politely. You both wrote careful texts and then stared at read receipts. Nobody wanted to be first to say 'I miss you', so nobody did. Underneath it all, you never felt quite enough as you were. The elegance is what pulls you, along with the hope that one day you'd finally pass inspection. Write a list of five things you love about yourself that nobody else would grade. Read it out loud. You were never a project. You were already in bloom.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, your eye for detail is a gift. Not every detail needs a note.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, you're not a bonsai. Stop letting people shape you.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Someone has to say 'I miss you' first. Usually it's the brave one.

im-water.title: River-fed vine, no fence
im-water.text: Your Im Water ex fed you like a river feeds a vine: fast, generous, a little wild. Links at 2am. Plans that changed by lunchtime. Ideas so big you felt bigger just standing near them. You grew quickly around them, and you adapted to every bend, so much that you lost track of what you wanted. When they disappeared into a project for days, it felt lonely, and you didn't say so, because you didn't want to be the one who needed things. Both of you love freedom, so the commitment conversation kept getting postponed, until it simply never happened. That's the strange shape of this breakup: it wasn't a fight, it was a riverbank that slowly eroded. The aliveness is what you crave. With them, life felt like a road trip without a map. Write down what you want from a relationship, separate from what they wanted, and pin it somewhere visible. And when someone goes dark for a day, ask instead of overthinking. Asking isn't clinging. It's watering your own roots.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, going dark for three days isn't mysterious. It's just dark.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, asking 'are we okay?' isn't clingy. It's clear.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Freedom is great. A commitment talk is also great. Try both.

gye-water.title: Dew on the petals, wished away
gye-water.text: You and your Gye Water ex spoke the same quiet language: song links, late-night thoughts, the kind of long messages that feel like a hand on your back. It was deeply kind. It was also very bad at problems. When something was wrong, neither of you said it. They got moody and withdrew; you tried to cheer them up, and when it didn't work, you quietly felt rejected. Plans dissolved because nobody set the direction. Money, logistics, the boring adult stuff floated in a fog until it turned into weather. It ended without a villain, two gentle people slowly drowning in what they didn't say. You miss feeling understood. They knew your moods before you did. Practise saying the important thing first and the soft thing second. 'I'm worried about rent. Also, here's a song.' Clarity is not the opposite of tenderness. In your case, it's what tenderness needed to survive. You can be the one who says it plainly and still be the one who sends the song.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, they tried so hard to make you smile. Tell people what actually helps.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, you can't sunshine your way out of somebody's weather.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say the hard thing clearly. Then add the song.
